definitions.gloss: sweet vinegar pickle; food pickled in sweetened vinegar
definitions.explanation: Vegetables, fish, or other ingredients preserved by soaking in a mixture of vinegar and sugar. A common side dish and garnish in Japanese cuisine.

examples.japanese: {大根|だいこん}の{甘酢漬|あまずづ}け。
examples.english: Daikon radish pickled in sweet vinegar.

examples.japanese: {新生姜|しんしょうが}の{甘酢漬|あまずづ}けを{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made sweet vinegar pickled ginger.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}は{野菜|やさい}の{甘酢漬|あまずづ}けをよく{食|た}べる。さっぱりしていて{食欲|しょくよく}が{出|で}る。
examples.english: In summer, I often eat vegetables pickled in sweet vinegar. They're refreshing and stimulate the appetite.

notes:
A compound of {甘酢|あまず} (sweet vinegar) + {漬|づ}け (pickle/preserved). The pickling liquid ({甘酢|あまず}) is a mixture of {酢|す} (vinegar), {砂糖|さとう} (sugar), and often {塩|しお} (salt).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大根|だいこん}の{甘酢漬|あまずづ}け: sweet vinegar pickled daikon
- {生姜|しょうが}の{甘酢漬|あまずづ}け: pickled ginger (like the pink ginger served with sushi)
- {甘酢漬|あまずづ}けにする: to pickle in sweet vinegar
- {野菜|やさい}の{甘酢漬|あまずづ}け: sweet vinegar pickled vegetables

CULTURAL NOTE:
The pink pickled ginger (ガリ) served alongside sushi is a type of {甘酢漬|あまずづ}け. {甘酢漬|あまずづ}け is also a popular way to preserve seasonal vegetables at home.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {漬物|つけもの}: pickles — the general term for all Japanese pickled foods
- {酢|す}の{物|もの}: vinegared dish — a broader category of vinegar-dressed dishes
- {南蛮漬|なんばんづ}け: nanban-zuke — fried food marinated in sweet vinegar with chili
